children: The South African rand edged up on Thursday, supported by a weaker dollar and firmer gold prices, as investors awaited a closely watched U.S. jobs report for clues on the Federal Reserve's next policy moves.
At 1450 GMT the rand traded at 16.0075 against the dollar
, about 0.3% stronger than its previous close.
South Africa's benchmark 2035 government bond (ZAR2035=) also strengthened, tracking higher gold prices, as the country is one of the world's major exporters of the precious metal.
The bond yield fell 7 basis points to 8.58%.
On the Johannesburg Stock Exchange, the Top-40 index
was last up 1.4%, with Impala Platinum
dipped 0.6% against a basket of currencies, easing pressure on emerging market currencies.
Investors now await the non-farm payrolls report due on Friday after the ADP employment report on Wednesday showed U.S. private payrolls increased moderately in August.
Like other risk-sensitive currencies, the rand often takes cues from global drivers like U.S. economic indicators, in addition to domestic economic data.
South African private sector activity expanded slightly in August as higher new orders supported output and purchasing, a business survey showed on Thursday.
